correctness.rationale: Step two on the index cycle has gcd(n,2) orbits of length n/gcd(n,2). The relation u_{i+2}=−u_i for u_i=x_i² forces origin in odd characteristic on odd-length orbits, and in characteristic two gives one free coordinate per orbit after reduction. When 4 divides n in odd characteristic, each parity is a cone of L=2^(n/2−1) distinct root-choice lines, normalized by its first coordinate; distinct lines intersect only at zero. Their Cartesian products are precisely the L² geometric components. A coefficient at the next position is ±sqrt(−1), so each nonsplit plane has quadratic field of definition, and over an odd-degree nonsplit extension any nonzero initial parity coordinate is impossible. Over a split extension of size Q each parity has 1+L(Q−1) points. Expanding the square gives L²Q²−2L(L−1)Q+(L−1)²; in the nonsplit base case its contribution is restricted to even degrees, with odd degrees giving 1. Formal summation using ∑T^r/r=−log(1−T) gives both quoted zeta formulas, including the factors at T=±1. The proof is for the reduced fiber, not radicality of the quadratic ideal. value.rationale: For the standard undirected cycle family, the zero-square fiber is a natural algebraic invariant. The complete arithmetic law quantifies a qualitative effect that geometric existence alone misses: exponentially many two-planes and yet no nonzero point until a quadratic extension. The formulas are a concrete finite-field benchmark and make the characteristic-two, split, and nonsplit behavior explicit without asserting a general graph result.
